name: J-PARC — Tokai accelerator complex
notes: Linked maps: no map:kamioka-observatory exists yet in this atlas; linked_map_ids is left empty here and the build's automatic derivation (from beamline:j-parc-neutrino's far_detector_site_ids) will populate it once the Kamioka campus has its own map.

facility:j-parc's notes record that the Materials and Life Science Experimental Facility (MLF, fed by the RCS) and a proposed muon g-2/EDM experiment are mentioned on official J-PARC pages, but neither has an atlas accelerator/beamline/detector/experiment record of its own (out of the HEP scope this atlas models), so neither appears in this map or in `unlocated[]` -- there is no entity id to list.

summary.plain: J-PARC's accelerator campus at Tokai, on Japan's Pacific coast: a linac, two synchrotron rings, the Hadron Experimental Facility, and the neutrino beamline that fires protons at a target and sends the resulting neutrino beam 295 km across Japan to Super-Kamiokande.
summary.technical: One local map for facility:j-parc covering the Tokai campus: the 400 MeV linac, 3 GeV RCS and 1567 m Main Ring tunnels (OSM indoor-mapped corridors, cross-checked against the T2K NIM paper's machine table), the Hadron Experimental Facility building (KOTO, COMET), the neutrino primary+secondary beamline tunnel and target station, the near-detector hall building (ND280, INGRID), and an inferred-direction line toward Super-Kamiokande.
